title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals — Docket Catalogue
content:
Every appeal under **Unemployment Insurance Appeals** is filed on one of seven dockets. A docket is fixed by the kind of record appealed and by who may appeal it; the docket in turn fixes the parties who are notified and may take part, whether related appeals of the same parties may be heard together, the order in which the docket is scheduled when hearing slots are short (1 is scheduled first), and the body to which the docket's decision may be appealed.

## What each docket hears

| Docket | Record appealed | Who may appeal | Issues heard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | a nonmonetary separation determination | the claimant or the separating employer | voluntary quit; discharge |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | a nonmonetary continuing-eligibility determination | the claimant | able and available; work search; refusal of work |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | a monetary determination or redetermination | the claimant or a base-period employer | wages; base period; weekly benefit amount |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | an overpayment determination | the claimant | overpaid amount; fault classification; fraud finding |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | a denial of charge relief | a base-period employer | chargeability; relief from charges |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | an annual rate notice or assessment | the employer | contribution rate; reserve ratio; experience transfer |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | a lower-authority decision, reviewed on the lower-authority hearing record | any party to the lower appeal | — |

## Parties, joint hearing, scheduling order and next level

| Docket | Interested parties notified and entitled to take part | Related appeals of the same parties may be heard together | Scheduling priority (1 first) | Decision may be appealed to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | the claimant and the separating employer | yes | 1 | the Board of Review |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | the claimant only | yes | 2 | the Board of Review |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | the claimant and the base-period employers | no | 3 | the Board of Review |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | the claimant only | yes | 4 | the Board of Review |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | the employer and the claimant | yes | 5 | the Board of Review |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | the employer only | no | 6 | the Board of Review |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | all parties to the lower-authority appeal | no | 7 | the circuit court |

## Reading the catalogue

- **Docket of an employer's appeal.** An employer contesting a denial of charge relief files on the Employer Benefit Charge docket; an employer contesting its annual rate notice or an assessment files on the Employer Contribution Rate docket; a separating employer contesting a separation determination files on the Separation Issue docket.
- **Docket of a claimant's appeal.** A claimant may appeal on the Separation Issue, Able and Available Issue, Monetary Determination and Overpayment and Fraud dockets. The Employer Benefit Charge and Employer Contribution Rate dockets list no claimant appellant, although the claimant is an interested party on the Employer Benefit Charge docket.
- **Joint hearing.** The Monetary Determination, Employer Contribution Rate and Board of Review dockets do not hear related appeals together; the other four lower-authority dockets do.
- **Two dockets compared (illustration).** When hearing slots are short, an Able and Available Issue appeal (priority 2) is scheduled ahead of an Employer Contribution Rate appeal (priority 6), and a Separation Issue appeal (priority 1) ahead of both.
- **Next level.** Every lower-authority docket's decision goes to the Board of Review; a Board of Review decision goes to the circuit court.
